# unordered-list-style

- ID: `MD004`
- Category: Lists
- Default: on, severity warning
- Fixable: yes
- Tags: `bullet`, `ul`
- Also named: `ul-style`, as in markdownlint

Every bullet uses the same marker as the first bullet in the file.

## Why

Mixed markers make the source harder to read. Inside a list, a different marker
also starts a new list.

## Options

Set them under `rules.unordered-list-style.options`.

- `style` (`string`, default `consistent`): Bullet to require. consistent takes
  the bullet of the first list, and sublist gives each nesting level a bullet
  that differs from its parent level's. Values: `consistent`, `asterisk`,
  `plus`, `dash`, `sublist`.

## Fix

The fix changes each marker to the expected one. gomdlint reports a list without
a fix when the new marker would merge it with a list next to it. gomdlint may
report a finding without a fix when the fix would change a line with one
character in brackets, such as \[x\] or \[1\], or the lines around it up to a
blank line, because it could add or remove a task list checkbox. In a document
with raw HTML other than comments and plain br, wbr, hr or img tags, gomdlint
reports every finding without a fix.

## Configure

```yaml
rules:
  unordered-list-style:
    options:
      style: consistent
```

Under `rules`, `unordered-list-style: false` turns the rule off and
`unordered-list-style: error` reports its findings as errors. The flag
`--disable unordered-list-style` turns it off for one run.

## Silence one line

```markdown
<!-- markdownlint-disable-next-line ul-style -->
```
